title: SAC Member Meetings
description:
SAC Members attend weekly meetings to stay up-to-date on organization activities, contribute to the planning of events, and get connected to members and campus community. 

Interested in becoming a member? Attend one of our weekly meetings led by our Executive Board team. An orientation for new members will be held at the end of the meeting - there you will learn about member expectations and what SAC is all about.

What to expect from a member meeting - 
  • SAC updates from President and VP of Membership
  • Event updates from Chairpersons
  • Opportunities to volunteer at events
  • Committee Breakouts
  • New member orientation

What happens in committee breakouts?

This is where the planning takes place. Our Chairpersons lead committee breakouts and you all brainstorm new ideas, make decisions, decide on creative marketing and set plans for your upcoming event.

Member Meetings occur every Monday from 3:30-5pm, and will exclude the following dates; 9/7, 10/12, 10/19, and 11/9. The meetings will help inform SAC general members about events, opportunities, and general updates within the organization, members also get a majority of the meeting to meet with their committee and discuss events. 

Let us know you are interested by completing a SAC Member Application

title: Songfest - Wrapped
description:
Get ready for the biggest, boldest, most unforgettable night on campus, Songfest is back! This high-energy lip sync and dance competition brings student orgs together to battle it out on stage with show-stopping choreography, creative themes, and crowd-pleasing performances. Cheer on your friends, rep your org, and witness the talent and teamwork that make this one of the most beloved traditions of the year. Lights. Music. Action. Are you ready to steal the show?  

This year’s Songfest theme is “Wrapped,” inspired by the end-of-year music recap experience made popular by Spotify Wrapped.

Groups are encouraged to create a performance that feels like a personalized music recap, highlighting songs, artists, trends, moments, or musical eras that defined the year. Your performance can tell a story, showcase a collection of songs, or take the audience through different “categories” of your own Wrapped experience.

This event is coordinated by Student Engagement & Belonging. For questions about this event, please call (316) 978-3022 or email greeklife@wichita.edu. To learn more about Fraternity and Sorority Life at Wichita State, visit www.wichita.edu/fsl.

title: The Greek Playbook - Recruitment Remix
description:
The Greek Playbook is designed to give FSL students practical tools, strategies, and knowledge they can take directly back to their organizations. This session will focus on what recruitment really means and how meaningful relationship contribute to the success of the chapter.
 
Recruitment is more than just getting new members; it's about building meaningful relationships and creating an experience that makes people want to be part of your organization! In this interactive workshop, fraternity and sorority leaders will challenge common recruitment myths, practice authentic conversations, and rethink how they connect with potential new members. Through creative activities and real-world scenarios, you'll explore how to make every interaction count, from the first conversation to a new member's first semester. Walk away with fresh ideas and three actionable strategies to take your chapter's recruitment experience to the next level!

title: Professional Networking Workshop
description:
Graduate Student Council & Student Government Association will be hosting Professional Networking Workshop that will be conducted by Shocker Career Accelerator! This event is free for all GRADUATE STUDENTS!

Description: Professional networking is more than collecting contacts. It is about building authentic relationships that support career growth and create opportunities. In this interactive workshop, students will explore how to identify and expand their network, engage confidently with professionals in a variety of settings, and maintain connections over time. Through guided activities and networking practice, participants will develop conversation strategies, learn techniques for professional events, and discover how to communicate experiences related to teamwork, leadership, and decision-making in ways that resonate with different audiences.

title: SAC Member Meetings
description:
SAC Members attend weekly meetings to stay up-to-date on organization activities, contribute to the planning of events, and get connected to members and campus community. 

Interested in becoming a member? Attend one of our weekly meetings led by our Executive Board team. An orientation for new members will be held at the end of the meeting - there you will learn about member expectations and what SAC is all about.

What to expect from a member meeting - 
  • SAC updates from President and VP of Membership
  • Event updates from Chairpersons
  • Opportunities to volunteer at events
  • Committee Breakouts
  • New member orientation

What happens in committee breakouts?

This is where the planning takes place. Our Chairpersons lead committee breakouts and you all brainstorm new ideas, make decisions, decide on creative marketing and set plans for your upcoming event.

Member Meetings occur every Monday from 3:30-5pm, and will exclude the following dates; 9/7, 10/12, 10/19, and 11/9. The meetings will help inform SAC general members about events, opportunities, and general updates within the organization, members also get a majority of the meeting to meet with their committee and discuss events. 

Let us know you are interested by completing a SAC Member Application

title: The Greek Playbook - Beyond the Group Chat
description:
The Greek Playbook is designed to give FSL students practical tools, strategies, and knowledge they can take directly back to their organizations. This session is all about chapter culture and ensuring your brotherhood/sisterhood can withstand anything. 

Strong brotherhood and sisterhood go beyond group chats, chapter meetings, and social events! In this interactive workshop, fraternity and sorority leaders will explore what it takes to build genuine connections, create a healthy chapter culture, and keep members engaged throughout their membership experience. Through honest conversations, creative challenges, and collaborative activities, you'll evaluate your chapter's strengths, identify opportunities for growth, and discover simple ways to strengthen relationships without breaking the budget. Walk away with fresh ideas and a Chapter Connection Challenge you can put into action within 30 days!
